person.name: Dong Hwi Kim
person.affiliation: Mechanical Engineering & Electrical and Computer Engineering · Seoul National University
person.intro: I am an undergraduate at Seoul National University studying Mechanical Engineering and Electrical and Computer Engineering. My interests span 3D vision and perception, control, robotics, and autonomous driving.
person.bio: At the RPM Robotics Lab, I work with Prof. Ayoung Kim on 3D Gaussian Splatting for SLAM and 3D mapping. At the AIDAS Lab, my collaboration with Prof. Jaeyoung Do focuses on visual data augmentation for robot learning using reconstructed scenes and robot kinematics.

sections.heading: Metric alignment without absorbing reconstruction errors
sections.body: Use calibrated geometry and rigid-part distances to set reconstruction scale before refining pose.

points.text: Compare distances between rigid robot parts with URDF dimensions. A Gaussian shell can bias nearest-surface or silhouette measurements.
Keep scale fixed and run point-to-point ICP on robot Gaussians with opacity at least 0.8.
Check the table footprint, cube dimensions, and robot rulers in the same metric frame.

figure.alt: Repository figure comparing robot length-ruler errors and Gaussian-core distances before and after scale correction
figure.caption: Rigid-part distances check metric scale. Measurements refer to the repository’s reference capture.

sections.heading: CAD-based link assignment and canonical assets
sections.body: Transform Gaussian centers into the robot base frame and query their distance to each sampled CAD link surface.

points.text: Assign each candidate to the nearest link. Mark candidates beyond the distance cap as background.
Apply inverse forward kinematics at the capture pose to create reusable articulated assets.
Reapply the capture pose and check that the original posed geometry is recovered.

sources.label: Inverse-FK export and geometry round trip

sections.heading: Separate trajectory planning from Gaussian rendering
sections.body: Replay joint and object states from a planned episode through the Gaussian scene.

points.text: Use forward kinematics to pose every robot-link asset at each timestep.
Replay object positions and orientations with explicit grasp attachment and release states.
Render two standing cameras and an FK-updated wrist camera from the same timestep.
Write camera images and robot/object state together for the dataset pipeline.

sources.label: Per-frame state replay and camera updates

figure.alt: Four rendered stages of the same FR3 cube-stacking episode
figure.caption: Approach, grasp, and stacking in a rendered episode. The montage illustrates kinematic replay.

sections.heading: Repair the geometry novel views expose
sections.body: Complete surfaces that were hidden or poorly reconstructed in the static capture.

points.text: Reconstruct a rolled capture separately and align matching cubes. Transplant the missing surface band with colors from the static capture.
Replace haze with a Gaussian sheet on the calibrated plane, bounded by the measured tabletop rectangle.

sources.label: Capture separation, surface transplant, and color transfer

sections.heading: Gate episodes before dataset export
sections.body: Validate geometry and rendered observations before accepting an episode.

points.text: Check finger spacing, object continuity, and the canonical-to-posed robot round trip.
Check black frames and per-object wrist visibility while an object is carried.

projects.title: Autonomous Object-Collecting Robot
projects.image_alt: Team 7's autonomous mecanum-wheel robot in the competition arena
projects.summary: A mecanum-wheel robot that converts dual-camera detections into object collection and return maneuvers.
projects.role: Contributed across perception and model training, planning, data collection, hardware, and system integration with Team 7.

sections.heading: Hardware and motion commands
sections.body: A Jetson Orin Nano handles perception and navigation. An ESP32 converts serial body-velocity commands into four wheel commands.

points.text: Calibrate wheel direction and feed-forward gains before combining forward, lateral, and rotational motion.
Attach a duration and auto-stop to motion commands.

sections.heading: Two cameras, one geometric view
sections.body: Run YOLO segmentation on both angled cameras and merge each camera cycle into one UDP message.

points.text: Use each camera’s focal length and mounting angle to express a detection in the robot’s forward-facing view.
Check confidence, predicted bearing, distance-normalized mask area, and arena-cell ownership before selecting an object.
Multiply mask area by squared relative range so the area gate accounts for apparent size changes.
Deduplicate same-class votes within each captured-frame group so overlapping camera views do not count twice.

sources.label: Windowed evidence filtering and frame-group voting

sections.formula:
bearing = camera toe angle + atan((c_x − W/2) / f_x)
normalized area = mask area × (range / reference range)²
sections.formula_note: c_x is the detection center, W is image width, and f_x is horizontal focal length. Bearing and area gates are applied by navigation, after detection.

sections.heading: Collection events and capacity-triggered return
sections.body: Follow the arena sweep and trigger collection from live target decisions.

points.text: The passive collector holds three objects. Forward motion captures; reverse motion can release the load.
Count collected objects across route segments. A full-basket event interrupts the current motion sequence.
The central controller reads a fresh stationary pose and drives the return route.
The forward path records return state. Autonomous unloading and forward-sweep resumption are not implemented in that path.

figure.alt: Official team repository diagram showing the object grid, storage corner, and robot start corner
figure.caption: Arena layout. The route links target collection to the delivery zone.

sections.heading: Geometry-based localization and calibrated control
sections.body: Fit the known rectangular arena to LiDAR points and estimate the robot’s pose from its walls.

points.text: Search wall orientation, refine the minimum-area fit, and use robust wall extents to reject distant returns.
Size a calibrated turn pulse and stop it using integrated IMU yaw.
Use LiDAR feedback for lateral motion. The less accurate timed alternative remains disabled by default.
Apply calibrated reverse pulses and keep cruise speed inside the measured braking range.

sections.heading: Perception and motion tested together
sections.body: Set detection thresholds for the number of observations available while the robot passes an object.

points.text: Benchmark on the Jetson. Scan speed determines how many detection frames reach the decision gate.
Detect frozen camera streams and save raw images alongside motion logs for diagnosis.

projects.title: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
projects.image_alt: Team MRI reconstruction framework using brain and knee experts with Feature VarNet and FI VarNet
projects.summary: Reconstruct undersampled MRI with acquisition-specific Feature/FI VarNet models and checkpoint averaging.

sections.heading: Rule-based expert routing
sections.body: Determine the acquisition condition before running its reconstruction model.

points.text: Treat 15-coil inputs as knee scans under this challenge’s data convention; route other inputs to brain models.
Remove the contiguous calibration region from the sampling-density calculation. Classify the remaining density as 4× or 8×.
Use these explicit rules to select the configured model or model pair.

rows: Mean of Feature VarNet and FI VarNet
Mean of Feature VarNet and FI VarNet
Mean of Feature VarNet and FI VarNet

sections.heading: Feature-domain reconstruction and data consistency
sections.body: Estimate coil sensitivities, combine the coil images, and encode them into learned features.

points.text: Run 12 feature cascades with 32 feature channels and an 8-channel sensitivity network.
Follow the 12 feature cascades with six image-domain cascades.
Share the feature encoder and decoder across cascades. Keep the cascade U-Nets separate and disable attention.
Decode the features into predicted k-space. Compute disagreement only at acquired samples and encode that residual back into features.
Subtract the learned correction and the weighted measurement-residual correction. Repeat before coil combination and output cropping.

sections.formula_note: M is the acquisition mask, y is measured multi-coil k-space, and k_pred is the current prediction. Each cascade uses this residual for a learned-weight data-consistency update.

sections.heading: Acquisition-aware data processing
sections.body: Prepare training examples for the target anatomy and acceleration.

points.text: Rebuild the mask for the chosen 4× or 8× setting before applying it to training k-space.
Transform the full and masked coil images together, then recompute k-space and the reconstruction target.
Use small rotations, shearing, and horizontal flips. Increase augmentation strength with the exponential schedule shown in the presentation.
Build an anatomy-specific target mask with thresholding, erosion, and dilation. Mask the prediction and target before computing SSIM loss.
The submission scripts pool the supplied training and validation splits for final training.

sections.heading: Training within the memory budget
sections.body: Combine activation checkpointing with DeepSpeed optimizer-state offloading where enabled.

points.text: Recompute intermediate activations during backpropagation instead of keeping every cascade’s activations in GPU memory.
The DeepSpeed path uses CPU Adam and offloads optimizer state to the CPU.
Resume the shared-acceleration brain models for 4× or 8× fine-tuning. Train separate knee experts.
Use warmup followed by cosine scheduling.

sections.heading: Checkpoint averaging and inference
sections.body: Average compatible checkpoints before combining model outputs.

points.text: Load checkpoint tensors on the CPU, average them in float32, and save one model state.
Weight averaging retains one forward pass per model. Output ensembling runs both selected models and averages their reconstructions.
Collect reconstructed slices by volume and write them in slice order for submission.

projects.title: Multimodal Scene Reordering
projects.image_alt: Diagram of mapping frame-order views into a common coordinate system for Random4 inference
projects.summary: Recover the chronological order of four shuffled images using a vision-language model.

sections.heading: Structured readouts from one model pass
sections.body: Adapt Qwen3.5-27B with language LoRA. Append ten readout positions after the sentence and four images.

points.text: Six readouts score which image comes earlier in each image pair.
Four readouts score the image identity at each position.
Read frame-label digit logits from the frozen language-model head instead of generating an answer string.

sources.label: Readout scaffold and frozen output head

sections.heading: Score all valid chronological orders
sections.body: Enumerate the 24 possible permutations and select the highest-scoring order.

points.text: Sum the log-probabilities of the image assigned to each chronological slot.
Use the difference between the two frame-label logits. Add or subtract it according to the candidate’s pair order.
Invert the selected image sequence to produce the per-input ranks required by the competition.

sections.formula: order score = slot log-probability + signed pairwise agreement

sections.heading: Align predictions across four input arrangements
sections.body: Evaluate the same sample under four image orderings before decoding.

points.text: Remap slot logits to the original image labels.
Remap pair identities and flip the signed score when a pair’s display order is reversed.
Average the aligned slot and pair logits, then run the same 24-permutation decoder.

sections.heading: Temporal supervision during fine-tuning
sections.body: Continue from the language adapter with temporal-gap and ranking objectives.

points.text: Predict the absolute chronological separation of each image pair. This auxiliary head is used only during training.
Compare the true sequence against adjacent swaps, a high-scoring medium-distance order, and full reversal.
Train the gap head first with the adapter frozen, then jointly fine-tune at a smaller adapter learning rate.

sections.heading: One averaged language adapter
sections.body: Average nine language-LoRA snapshots from the same training trajectory.

points.text: Average LoRA A/B tensors on the CPU in float32 and cast them back to the stored dtype.
Use one averaged adapter with the frozen base model. The training-only gap head is excluded.
Parameter averaging adds no extra forward passes; Random4 still evaluates four input arrangements.

projects.title: Physics-Guided Wind Power Forecasting
projects.image_alt: Zephyr Analytics team cover for the 2025 Wind Power Prediction Competition
projects.summary: Forecast hourly wind generation by correcting a physical power curve with learned residuals.
projects.role: Model architecture design and hyperparameter optimization.

sections.heading: Physical baseline
sections.body: Estimate generation from weather conditions and the turbine power curve.

points.text: Use weather and turbine characteristics to compute an initial power-curve forecast.
Subtract this estimate from observed generation to form the residual training target.

sections.heading: Residual learning
sections.body: Train LightGBM to predict the difference between observed generation and the physical baseline.

points.text: Subtract the baseline forecast from the observed generation.
Add the learned correction back to the physical estimate.

sections.formula:
residual target = observed generation − physical forecast
hybrid forecast = physical forecast + predicted residual

sections.heading: Ensemble and hyperparameter optimization
sections.body: Combine the hybrid model with Ridge Regression and Random Forest forecasts.

points.text: Use Optuna to select model hyperparameters.
Optimize the weighted combination of the hybrid, Ridge Regression, and Random Forest forecasts.
Inspect site-wise prediction distributions as well as aggregate error and settlement revenue.

projects.title: Automated Filming Device
projects.image_alt: Sunflower-inspired face-tracking camera device with a yellow phone mount and white circular base
projects.summary: A Raspberry Pi camera mount with automatic face tracking and infrared remote control.

sections.heading: Hardware
sections.body: A Raspberry Pi connects the camera, two servos, and infrared receiver.

points.text: Rotate the camera horizontally and vertically with separate servo axes.
Use a ball-transfer unit to distribute weight and reduce friction.

figure.alt: Exploded hardware diagram of the pan–tilt filming device
figure.caption: Camera mount, two servo axes, and ball-transfer support.

sections.heading: Pixel error to incremental servo motion
sections.body: Capture frames with Picamera2, run the Haar-cascade face detector, and select the largest detected face.

points.text: Measure the selected face center relative to the image center and normalize by image width and height.
Multiply each normalized error by a proportional gain of 30 to obtain the incremental servo-angle command.
Add the increment to the current angle, clamp it to the servo limits, and map it to calibrated pulse width.
Skip automatic updates when no valid face center is available and turn off the detection LED.

sources.label: Face selection, error computation, and servo output

sections.formula:
e_x = (W/2 − c_x) / W; e_y = (H/2 − c_y) / H
Δθ_pan = 30 e_x; Δθ_tilt = 30 e_y
sections.formula_note: W and H are image dimensions; c_x and c_y are the face center. The released controller sets both derivative gains to zero.

figure.alt: Team diagram of the filming device software and control flow
figure.caption: Team software design. The controller description here follows the final implementation.

sections.heading: Concurrent remote control and shutdown
sections.body: Run the LIRC infrared reader in a separate thread alongside the camera loop.

points.text: KEY_0 switches automatic tracking on or off.
Directional keys start continuous motion on either axis; KEY_5 stops the servos.
KEY_9 ends the loop. Reset the camera pose, stop capture, disable servo pulses, and join the remote thread.

projects.title: TaXer and WaXer: Time-Series Forecasting
projects.image_alt: Original presentation slide showing the TaXer periodic feature extraction and cross-attention architecture
projects.summary: Combine a transformer forecaster with periodic or dilated-convolution temporal features.

sections.heading: TaXer: learn temporal context from dominant periods
sections.body: Pass the input window through a TimesNet feature extractor before the forecasting transformer.

points.text: Use FFT amplitudes to select dominant periods and reshape the sequence into within-period and across-period axes.
Apply the TimesNet 2D convolution blocks, then project their output to the transformer embedding dimension.
Broadcast the projected temporal context to each variable’s forecasting branch.

sources.label: FFT period detection and periodic feature blocks

sections.heading: Global-token cross-attention
sections.body: Normalize each variable’s input window and split it into patch tokens plus one global token.

points.text: Model relationships among patches within each variable branch.
Use the global token as the query and the projected temporal features as keys and values.
Flatten the updated patch/global-token representation and project it to the prediction horizon.
Restore the input window’s per-variable mean and standard deviation after prediction.

sections.formula: Q = global token; K, V = projected temporal features
sections.formula_note: The auxiliary context comes from the same input window. It is an extracted representation rather than an additional measured sensor stream.

sections.heading: WaXer: replace the temporal prior
sections.body: Use a WaveNet feature extractor through the same projection and cross-attention interface.

points.text: Increase dilation as 1, 2, 4, … and trim right padding to exclude future samples.
Multiply tanh-filter and sigmoid-gate outputs. Combine residual paths with accumulated skip features.
Feed these features into the same variable-wise transformer and forecasting head.

sources.label: Dilated gated convolution and skip paths
